subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should unconfigured memory search get a default periodic sync fallback when watcher events may be missed?
rationale: The bug is real at the source level, but changing the default from no periodic sync to background rescans can affect existing users with filesystem, embedding-provider, and upgrade-cost implications.

options.title: Approve a repaired default fallback
options.body: Land the linked PR after scoping dirty marking correctly and accepting the 30-minute default-on interval fallback as the upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep periodic sync opt-in
options.body: Preserve the `0` default and document or doctor-recommend `intervalMinutes: 30` as the workaround for users who need watcher-outage protection.

options.title: Request a watcher-health design
options.body: Pause the default change and require a narrower watcher liveness or recovery mechanism before changing sync policy.

recommendation.title: Approve a repaired default fallback
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR after scoping dirty marking correctly and accepting the 30-minute default-on interval fallback as the upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory/config refactors and current shallow blame make steipete the best available owner for the default/fallback product decision.
